correctness.rationale: The Cayley substitution gives t+t^{-1}=2(1+z)/(1-z) for t=(1+sqrt(z))/(1-sqrt(z)). In characteristic p, Frobenius expansion of (1±sqrt(z))^(p^r+1) gives the claimed homogenized polynomial 2(1+z^d). Its roots are distinct and avoid 1 and infinity. Independently of the cited geometric theorem, the Hessian determinant of Z^d+W^d is a nonzero constant times (ZW)^(d-2), since d and d-1 are nonzero modulo p. A projectivity preserving the reduced divisor preserves the homogeneous form up to scale, so Hessian covariance forces it to preserve the pair {0,infinity}. The resulting rotations and inversions are exactly the stated D_d. Descent uses trivial H^1 of PGL_2 over a finite field; every dihedral cocycle value is allowed because the semidirect product by the finite-order Frobenius action is finite. Cocycle conjugation by (c,delta) sends a to delta(a+(epsilon Q-1)c). This yields exactly the two quotient-and-inversion sectors and the stabilizer conditions, with any descending reflection squaring to one and inverting the rotation subgroup. Writing z_j=eta^(2j+1) yields the affine action; iterating and solving the fixed-point congruence gives the formula for every extension. For d=6,Q=11 the + sector produces cycle types 2^3 and 1^2 2^2; the − sector is translation by a=0,1,2,3 and gives 1^6, 6, 3^2, 2^3, independently confirming the five stated zeta functions.
residual_risks: Labels use a chosen primitive root and coordinate; uniqueness is for the chosen parametrization, not intrinsic naming.

value.rationale: This supplies explicit descent invariants for a distinguished family of branch divisors, not simply a new proof of the geometric dihedral group. It makes possible the independent tasks of counting embeddings up to rational projectivity, finding rational symmetries, and obtaining every extension-field count. The six-form example demonstrates a meaningful distinction: scheme zeta data can agree although projective forms differ. The elementary group calculation is valuable as a complete classification with computable stabilizer and cycle information.
residual_risks: No equations for all descended divisors or data on covers or Jacobians are supplied. Interest is in the arithmetic forms of this specific family.
